title: OSHA Hot Work Fire Watch Checklist (29 CFR 1926.352)
subtitle: Use before and after each hot work job on site.
instructions: Mark every item OK, Defect or N/A before hot work starts; recheck section B after the work ends.
If any item is a Defect, don't start or continue the work until it is corrected, and record what was done.
Manufacturer's instructions and site rules may add checks to this list.

sections.title: Work location and surrounding fire hazards
items: Where moving it was practical, the object being worked on sits in a designated safe location.
Where the object stays put, every movable fire hazard nearby has been taken to a safe place or protected.
Where the object and some hazards can't be moved, positive means are in place that confine heat, sparks and slag and protect the immovable hazards.
No flammable paints, compounds or heavy dust
No flammable paint being applied, no other flammable compounds and no heavy dust concentrations creating a hazard at the work point.
Opposite side of walls, floors and ceilings
For work on a wall, floor or ceiling, the adjacent side has the same precautions as the working side.

sections.title: Fire extinguishing equipment and fire watch
items: Suitable fire extinguishing equipment is in the work area itself and immediately available.
Extinguishing equipment is in a state of readiness for instant use when checked.
Where normal precautions aren't sufficient, extra personnel are assigned to guard against fire for the whole time the work is performed.
Fire watch stays after the work
Fire guard remains after completion until there is no possibility of fire.
Fire guard can name the specific anticipated fire hazards and explain how to use the firefighting equipment provided.

sections.title: Torches and hoses in enclosed spaces
items: Gas shut off outside the space
Torch gas supply is positively shut off at a point outside the enclosed space whenever the torch is not in use or left unattended for a substantial period, such as lunch.
Torch and hose out overnight and at shift change
No torch or hose left inside the confined space overnight or at the change of shifts.
Open-end fuel gas and oxygen hoses are taken out of the enclosed space as soon as they are disconnected from the torch or other gas-consuming device.

sections.title: Drums, containers and hollow structures
items: Drums, pails and other containers that hold or held flammable liquids are closed unless contents are being removed or transferred.
Empty containers are in a safe area apart from hot work and open flames.
Vessels filled or cleaned, ventilated and tested
Before hot work, any drum, container or hollow structure that held toxic or flammable substances is either filled with water or thoroughly cleaned, ventilated and tested.
For steel pipelines containing natural gas, the work follows the pertinent portions of 49 CFR part 192.
A vent or opening is in place on the drum, container or hollow structure before heat is applied, to release built-up pressure.

references: 29 CFR 1926.352: Fire prevention (Part 1926 Subpart J, Welding and Cutting)
49 CFR part 192: Minimum Federal Safety Standards for Gas Pipelines (referenced by 1926.352(i))
